title: Instrument RBAC policy bundle updates with audit events + diffs (role create/update/delete, permission changes)
creator: Naomi Feldman
description:
Context
- Audit logging program requires 100% coverage for sensitive actions. RBAC changes are top-tier sensitive actions (directly impact customer data access and security posture).
- This ticket instruments RBAC policy bundle operations (role + permission changes) with canonical audit events per audit-event-schema-v1.

In scope
1) Role lifecycle
- Create role
- Update role metadata (name, description)
- Delete role

2) Permission/assignment changes (the policy bundle)
- Add/remove permissions from a role
- Add/remove users/service accounts/groups to/from a role (if represented in the bundle)
- Changes to built-in/default roles (where allowed) must be logged, even if action is denied (outcome=fail) for attempted changes.

3) "Who changed what" diff
- Include structured before/after for the relevant RBAC objects.
- Diff must be human-debuggable and machine-queryable for compliance evidence.

Non-goals / out of scope (for this ticket)
- Logging every authz decision (non-sensitive, too high-volume)
- Full historical backfill of RBAC change events prior to schema v1
- UI work in Console to render diffs nicely (tracked elsewhere)

Proposed audit event names (naming per api-standards/audit-event-naming-guidelines)
- rbac.role.create
- rbac.role.update
- rbac.role.delete
- rbac.role.permissions.update  (use when the primary change is permission set)
- rbac.role.assignments.update  (use when the primary change is member bindings)

Notes:
- If the API endpoint is a single "policy bundle update" that can include multiple changes, we should emit:
  - One top-level event for the bundle update (rbac.policy_bundle.update) OR
  - Multiple more-specific events per entity changed.
Decision: Emit ONE event per request, with a diff payload listing changes by category. This avoids event spam while preserving detail. Event name will be rbac.policy_bundle.update.

Canonical sensitive actions covered by this ticket
- "Modify roles or permissions" (create/update/delete)
- "Change who has access" (role assignments)

Schema requirements (audit-event-schema-v1)
- Required envelope fields must be present: event_name, event_version, emitted_at, org, workspace (if applicable), actor, request_id, ip, user_agent, outcome, and target.
- Actor attribution rules:
  - Console-initiated changes: actor.type=user, include actor.user_id and actor.email (if allowed), plus session_id when available.
  - API-initiated changes: actor.type=api_key (or service_account) with key_id / service account id.
  - Service-initiated changes (automation): actor.type=service with service.name, and MUST include an "initiating_actor" field if the service is acting on behalf of a user request.

Target modeling
- target.type should be "rbac_policy_bundle" for bundle-level updates.
- Include target.id = policy bundle id (or org id if that’s the stable identifier).
- Include target.subresources in payload for roles/assignments affected.

Diff payload (required)
- event.payload.rbac_diff:
  - roles_created: list of role identifiers + display name
  - roles_deleted: list of role identifiers + display name
  - roles_updated: list, with per-role changed_fields and before/after
  - permissions_added: list of {role_id, permission}
  - permissions_removed: list of {role_id, permission}
  - assignments_added: list of {role_id, principal_type, principal_id}
  - assignments_removed: list of {role_id, principal_type, principal_id}
- Redaction: do not include secrets, raw tokens, or session cookies. Emails are allowed only if policy permits; prefer stable ids.

Error/outcome semantics
- outcome=success when persisted change succeeded.
- outcome=fail for rejected updates (validation, forbidden, conflict). Include error_type (e.g., forbidden, validation_error) and a safe error_message.
- outcome=unknown only if request outcome cannot be determined (should be rare; needs follow-up if observed).

Acceptance criteria
- [x] For each RBAC bundle update request, exactly one audit event is emitted with event_name=rbac.policy_bundle.update.
- [x] Event includes request_id and traces across gateway -> RBAC service.
- [x] Actor is correctly populated for console, api key, and service-initiated changes.
- [x] Diff payload includes before/after details sufficient to answer: "who changed what, when".
- [x] Redaction tests verify no secrets/tokens are included.
- [x] Integration tests (ENG-2492) cover at least: role create, permission add/remove, role assignment add/remove.
- [x] Event passes schema validation and registry checks (ENG-2482).

Implementation notes
- Hook point: RBAC policy bundle write path (post-commit preferred to avoid logging changes that roll back).
- Construct diff using normalized RBAC model (avoid raw request payload diff; too noisy and may include irrelevant fields).
- Emit event after successful commit; for failure cases, emit from error handler with partial diff computed from attempted change.

Open questions
1) Bundle update endpoint can include multiple org/workspace scopes. Confirm canonical scope fields (org_id required; workspace_id optional).
2) Are group principals supported in this bundle? If yes, principal_type should include "group".
3) Should we include role name strings in payload for readability? Security review requested: ok to include role display names (not sensitive) but avoid user-provided freeform descriptions if they can contain PII.

References
- Program: Audit log schema standardization + coverage
- Related work: ENG-2481 (schema), ENG-2482 (library + registry), ENG-2492 (integration tests)
- Related PR (implementation): PR redwood#18466

Rollout plan
- Stage behind feature flag AUDIT_RBAC_BUNDLE_EVENTS (default on in staging).
- Dual-write legacy event (if any) only if required by migration plan; otherwise emit schema-v1 only.
- Enable in prod for 5% orgs for 24h (monitor delivery lag/drop dashboards), then 100%.
